policy: Native original JPEG; at least 3840x2160; no enlargement or recompression
review: All 240 candidates reviewed in eight contact sheets; 30 softest candidates additionally inspected in 1:1 center crops. Rejected watermarked, non-photographic, overly soft, non-autumn, visually repetitive and off-theme frames. Kept red/orange foliage, New England roads, villages, covered bridges and Pacific Northwest forests, with a few intentional mist/bokeh photographs. Native original JPEG bytes retained; sharpness at a common 768-pixel preview scale is a diagnostic, not a universal quality claim. Perceptual duplicate threshold: at most 12 differing bits in a 256-bit difference hash.

photos.title: File:Münster, Park Sentmaring -- 2015 -- 9923.jpg
photos.description: Branch of a horse chestnut in Sentmaring park in autumn, Münster, North Rhine-Westphalia, GermanyThe name is derived from “Park am ehemaligen Haus Sentmaring” (Park at the former Sentmaring House). However, the Sentmaring House, which gave the park its name, was demolished in 2003, along with its outbuildings. The garden has remained a landscape park. Part of the moat and a small cemetery east of the old moat have been preserved. On the west side of the park, directly adjacent to the busy federal highway 219 (Weseler Straße), a neo-baroque garden gate has been preserved. The landscape park itself was created in the 19th century.

photos.title: File:Dülmen, St.-Viktor-Kirche -- 2015 -- 9906.jpg
photos.description: Entry of the St Viktor Church in Dülmen, North Rhine-Westphalia, GermanyThe Roman Catholic parish church of St. Victor is the oldest church in Dülmen. It is located in the town center and is the only one within the former town walls. It was founded in 780 by Abbot Bernrad or St. Liudger on a Saxon (later episcopal) main farmstead. It is not only considered the original parish church of Dülmen, but also one of the oldest churches in the diocese of Münster. The church is named after and dedicated to St. Victor. The consecration of a larger church, which was probably the first stone church, took place in 1074. The church building was destroyed, rebuilt, renovated, or remodeled several times, but was always oriented toward the east, the place of sunrise. The church took on its current form around 1500, but was destroyed on March 21 and 22, 1945, and then rebuilt, with traces of the difficult reconstruction still visible.

photos.title: File:Dülmen, Wildpark, Brücke am Herzteich -- 2022 -- 4642.jpg
photos.description: Bridge at the heart pond in the wildlife park in Dülmen, North Rhine-Westphalia, GermanyThe wildlife park was designed in 1864 by English landscape architect Edward Milner as the “Amended Plan of Park Dülmen Westphalia” and laid out in 1868 by Charles Barnard, a gardener who also came from England. It is a classic landscape park with extensive meadows and a system of circular paths, which is also used for forestry. The park features the Herzteich pond with a small island, the moat of the former Schultenhof Hinderkinck farm, and a forester’s lodge near the moat. At the end of the 19th century, among other things, the park was expanded through the acquisition of additional properties. With the construction of the Bundesautobahn 43 in the 1970s, it was reduced in size by approximately 250 hectares.

Surrounding trees, adorned with the season's signature orange leaves, frame the dwelling from the back and the left front, evoking a blend of nature and nostalgia.
